title: Tools and agents
subtitle: When the model asks for help (and when it can’t stop)
mission: Give the agent tools to solve a sum and tell the time in another country. Then get it stuck trying something that doesn’t work.

predict.question: guess: the agent has a calculator. You ask what 23 x 47 is. It…

options.tool: Calls the calculator and uses the result
options.head: Does it “in its head”, word by word
options.refuse: Refuses, since it’s just a text model

feedback.right: exactly! The model doesn’t execute anything itself: it writes a request (“call the calculator with 23 x 47”), the program around it runs it and hands back the result. That’s the agent loop.
feedback.wrong: close! Look at the trace: the model writes a request for the calculator, the surrounding program runs it and returns the result. The model only decides and reads.
feedback.skipped: no guess? Look at the trace: think, call the tool, observe the result, answer. That’s the agent loop.

coach.ui: guess noted. Keep all three tools ticked and hit Run.
coach.cmd: guess noted. Run the command below: all three tools are on.

tryNext.ui: Now untick the calculator and run again. Compare the number with the previous one.
tryNext.cmd: Now run with --tools clock,search (no calculator) and compare the number.

why.simples:
The model is great with words and bad at sums and clocks. So we give it a toolbox. It doesn’t use the tool with its own hands: it asks “calculator, what’s 23 x 47?”, someone presses the buttons and tells it the result.
An agent is that, repeated: think, ask, see the answer, think again.
why.dev:
Tool calling: you describe the tools (name, what they do, parameters as JSON Schema). The model replies with a structured call; your code runs it, returns the result as a message, and the model continues.
An agent is that cycle in a loop, until the model answers or hits a step limit. The limit isn’t a detail: without it, a tool that always fails becomes an infinite loop (and an infinite token bill).
why.especialista:
In production the loop needs: step and cost limits, timeouts and retries with backoff, idempotent tools (or human confirmation for actions that spend money or delete things) and a log of every call.
Fewer, well-described tools usually beat many. Treat every tool output as untrusted input: a fetched page can carry instructions for the agent (indirect prompt injection).

mission.ui: time to break it. Pick “Will it rain in Lisbon tomorrow?” and run. Search is down today…
mission.cmd: time to break it. Run agent "Will it rain in Lisbon tomorrow?". Search is down today…

break.success: Broken: search failed, the agent retried, and again, until it hit the {max}-step limit. Without that limit it would keep trying forever, and every attempt costs.
break.calm: The agent finished in {cycles} of {max} steps. To break it, ask for something that depends on a failing tool: the weather.

ui: Tick the tools the agent may use and hit Run.
“Step limit” is how many loops the agent may take before giving up.
To break it: ask about the weather (search is down).
cmd: The task goes in quotes, after agent.
agent "Will it rain in Lisbon tomorrow?" --steps 4

errors.notInEnum.tools: “{value}” isn’t a tool here. Options: {options}. For none, use --tools none.
errors.aboveMax.maxSteps: Up to 10 steps. An agent with too high a limit is an agent with too high a bill.
errors.belowMin.maxSteps: At least 1 step, or the agent never starts.
errors.notInteger.maxSteps: Steps is a whole number, like --steps 4.

scene.label: The agent’s trace
scene.empty: Run to see the agent think and act.

phrases.noTask: I didn’t understand the task. I can do sums (23 x 47), tell the time in a city and try to check the weather.
phrases.thinkCalc: I need to compute {expr}. Sums are better on the calculator.
phrases.guessCalc: No calculator. I’ll estimate word by word… about {guess}.
phrases.thinkTime: I need the current time in {city}.
phrases.guessTime: Without a clock, I can’t know what time it is now.
phrases.answerTimeGuess: I don’t know the time in {city}: I need a clock.
phrases.thinkWeather: I need the weather forecast for {city}.
phrases.noSearch: Without search, I can’t know the weather.
phrases.answerNoWeather: I can’t check the weather in {city} without the search tool.
phrases.limit: Stopped: hit the {max}-step limit without finishing.

steps: In an AI chat with no tools (or with search off), ask: “What time is it in Tokyo right now?”.
Then, in a chat that shows tool use (search, code or calculator), ask: “Compute 23 x 47 using the code tool and show what you ran”.
recipe.ok: without a tool, it says it doesn’t know the current time (or gets it wrong); with the tool, the executed call shows up with the result 1,081.
